steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: I'm back.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: ...Luna? Are you there?
There's no response from inside the room, but Lavinia looks around and finds who she's looking for at the desk in the corner.
The table is stacked with books that have been read, and sleeping at the center of the books is the girl hunched over at the desk.

steps.name: Sleeping Girl
steps.text: Papà...

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Luna.

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: Hmm... Huh?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Sorry, did I wake you?

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: I... fell asleep?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: You sure did.

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: I finished this book today, Lavinia.

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: I read the notes you wrote in it, and left my own comments too.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: That's amazing. It took me a month to get through that one when I was a student, but you only took a week.

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: I thought I may as well study at home since I don't have a school to go to anymore.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: I'm sorry... The new city still needs some time to sort out its resources, particularly education.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: I'll make sure you get enrolled in a new one as soon as I can.

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: It's not your fault.

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: After what padre did, I didn't want to go to that school anymore anyway.

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: I should be thanking you instead, Lavinia. For taking me in.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: I promised him I would. Besides, there's no way I could just watch Segretario Rubio's daughter live out on the streets.

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: ...Actually, I don't care if I can't go back to school.

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: I mean, everyone already knows I'm his daughter.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: ...You had a long study session. You should take a break. I'll make dinner.

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: It's fine, I'm not tired. I'll help you out.

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: ...Do you know why I know how to cook?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Why?

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: Padre used to do two things as Segretario di Sicurezza Alimentare. Walk around the markets, and cook for the famiglie.

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: When he cooked for the famiglie, he usually had to keep his guests company so he couldn't cook for me and mamma.

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: Mamma didn't like to cook, so he taught me how.

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: And I was usually the one who made our meals.

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: I used to scold padre in my head whenever I cooked.

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: I still do.
The kitchen knife streaks across the moist scallions as it makes contact with the chopping board.

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: Stupid idiot... Why did he have to do that...

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Are you still unwilling to forgive him?

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: Does it matter? He's not coming back anyways.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: ...It's alright, Luna.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: I'll be with you.

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: Sorry... I... I... don't know.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: ...We'll visit Famiglia Saluzzo tomorrow and put an end to this.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: You are his daughter, so legally you have the right to do this.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Though I won't force you to go if you don't want to.

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: ...I'm going.

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: Padre was stupid, but I'd feel bad letting the Saluzzos keep his body.

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: You want a proper end to this whole thing too, right?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Whatever our reasons may be, the Saluzzos still owe us an explanation.
The famous magnanimous judge of Volsinii is gracing us with a visit today?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: I thought I'd find Don Alberto here.
The Don is no longer in Volsinii.
But he did expect someone to come asking for Rubio's body, so he specially instructed us to offer you our hospitality.
Though I didn't think you'd bring little Luna along.

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: ...I've seen you before. You used to work under mio padre.

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: You remember me? Wonderful. Just call me Teresa.

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: So you're part of the Saluzzos?

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: Yes, and it was no secret to Rubio.

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: Don't worry, Signorina Lavinia. The Don emphasized that we must wrap this matter up nicely.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Do you think it's 'nice' for us to have to personally knock on your door to get Segretario Rubio's body?

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: How could you say that?

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: His death was extremely troublesome for us, you know.

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: Oh, my apologies, dear. I didn't mean to hurt your feelings.

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: He was a very friendly boss to work under; everyone thought so. We were all upset by his death as well.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: We didn't come here to talk about this.

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: But Your Honor, wouldn't you agree with me?

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: His speech may have been quite moving, and even today I can still hear that gunshot going off.

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: But... it's been a while since then, and nothing has changed.

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: It seems to me everything's the same as ever.

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: The only thing that's different is a child lost her father.

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: Have you been well, dear?

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: ...Lavinia takes good care of me.

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: Good, good to hear.

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: However, Her Honor is a VIP in our new city with many affairs to tend to, so I don't see her having free time to play with you.

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: *sigh* How callous of your father. To throw you away along with his own life, all for nothing.

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: You think padre died for nothing?

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: I don't want to lie to you.

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: Let's say we hand over the reins of the new city to that Bellone boy and our dear judge here. What could they possibly achieve?

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: Your Honor, do you truly believe you can build a city free of the famiglie?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: We did not come here to debate with you, Signorina Teresa. Only to retrieve her father's body.

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: Of course, of course.

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: Bring them both to Rubio's remains.

steps.name: Radical Mafioso
steps.text: Come with me, you two.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Don't let her get to you, Luna.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: She's just trying to provoke us.

steps.name: Radical Mafioso
steps.text: Can you really say that, Signorina?

steps.name: Radical Mafioso
steps.text: Shouldn't you know better than anyone the weight of what she was saying?

steps.name: Radical Mafioso
steps.text: It doesn't matter what you or Signor Leontuzzo think of your own capabilities. Your goals just seem so ridiculous.

steps.name: Radical Mafioso
steps.text: You can't possibly think to defeat the famiglie with a slogan or two. Or do you really think Signora Sicilia likes you that much?

spans.text: You can't possibly think to defeat the famiglie with a slogan or two. Or do you really think Signora Sicilia likes you

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: You think padre died for nothing?

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: I don't want to lie to you.

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: Let's say we hand over the reins of the new city to that Bellone boy and our dear judge here. What could they possibly achieve?

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: Your Honor, do you truly believe you can build a city free of the famiglie?

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: (Muttering) I'm sorry, Lavinia.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Of course you wouldn't understand. 'Fairness' is not a word in a mafioso's dictionary.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: We may have to borrow Signora Sicilia's power for now, but we will prove to her that we won't need it forever.

steps.name: Radical Mafioso
steps.text: Bold words, but the girl doesn't seem to agree.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Luna...

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Luna?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Where is she?!

steps.name: Radical Mafioso
steps.text: Kill some time with us, Signorina.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: WHAT DID YOU DO TO HER?!

steps.name: Radical Mafioso
steps.text: Oh, don't get the wrong idea. We didn't touch her; she left you on her own.

steps.name: Radical Mafioso
steps.text: Our job is just to stop you from finding her.

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: I knew you'd be back.

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: My dear little Luna.

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: Come, let's talk. About your padre.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: What are you talking about...?

steps.name: Radical Mafioso
steps.text: Did you really think the Saluzzos would leave things be?

steps.name: Radical Mafioso
steps.text: All of us detest the Bellones. And you. And Rubio.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: So you devised this scheme to threaten me, with Luna as a hostage?

steps.name: Radical Mafioso
steps.text: Threaten?

steps.name: Radical Mafioso
steps.text: *tsk* *tsk* I see you still don't know us well enough, Signorina.

steps.name: Radical Mafioso
steps.text: We know people like you. We could kill someone you love right before your eyes, and you wouldn't even consider revenge.

steps.name: Radical Mafioso
steps.text: So more... unusual methods are required.

steps.name: Radical Mafioso
steps.text: Our little Luna should be with Teresa by now.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: You mean—

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: You dare—?!

steps.name: Radical Mafioso
steps.text: Haha. Bingo, Your Honor.

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: I don't get it. How?

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: How can you talk about padre's death so lightly?

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: Because life and death are everyday matters for us.

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: One day you're telling a joke, and the next you're gone forever.

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: You get used to it.

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: I don't want to.

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: Then you might just join the ones who disappear for good.

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: That gunshot may have caused some misconceptions, and you might have thought your father died a hero.

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: But give it a few days, months, years—will anyone actually remember what he did?

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: The sound of the rain silences everything, eventually.

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: Lavinia said she'll remember, and some other people too. That's enough.

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: And you believe her?

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: If you really, truly do—if you don't doubt her at all... then why did you come to me?

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: You do have doubts, don't you?

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: Even if Rubio's wish can come true, how much time will it take?

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: Can you afford to wait that long?

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: Or perhaps I should be asking: Are you willing to wait, my dear?

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: I—

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: Let's be serious, ragazzina.

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: You don't actually understand what Rubio was talking about.

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: You don't care either. How could you, at your age?

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: Honestly, shouldn't the target of your hate be our dear judge instead?

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: She lied to you.

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: About being patient. That what Rubio said could come true. I mean, consider this... what if she was the one who made him do all that in the first place?

spans.text: About being patient. That what Rubio said could come true. I mean, consider this... what if
was the one who made him do all that in the first place?

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: How much more blood will be spilled on the streets, all for our righteous lady of justice's ideals?

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: I won't let you talk about her that way!

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: But you do have doubts, no?

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: Let's make a deal then, shall we?

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: I'll hand over your father's corpse to Signorina Lavinia.

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: We only ask that you put in some nice words for us in any subsequent court hearings.

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: Rubio killed himself. Saluzzo had nothing to do with his suicide.

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: ...Just how much do you have to belittle mio padre and Lavinia until you're satisfied?

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: Belittle? I'm just stating the facts.

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: I mean, do you not loathe your father for leaving you behind?

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: You're wrong—

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: I do hate him for dying on his own and leaving me behind.

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: But I also know I should hate you guys even more.

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: The famiglia who drove him to his death!!!
Luna rips her backpack open to grab her hidden crossbow, and aims it at Teresa.
Teresa meets the cold crossbow bolt with a smile.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: From the very start... you planned to lure Luna into killing Teresa.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Are you people mad?! Willingly sending one of your own to die?!

steps.name: Radical Mafioso
steps.text: Mad? Us?

steps.name: Radical Mafioso
steps.text: To us, Rubio was the madman.

steps.name: Radical Mafioso
steps.text: He dragged us all down for his insane, impossible fantasy.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: You don't know the first thing about Segretario Rubio!

steps.name: Radical Mafioso
steps.text: You're right, we have no idea what he was talking about. But we do know how to deal with people like you.

steps.name: Radical Mafioso
steps.text: Relax, we have no plans to rub you out. But you better not get any ideas about finding the girl either.

steps.name: Radical Mafioso
steps.text: Just sit tight here till it's all over, and then we can go get Teresa's body.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Why?! Is Teresa that willing to throw her life away?!

steps.name: Radical Mafioso
steps.text: She was pretty unlucky to be Rubio's subordinate.

steps.name: Radical Mafioso
steps.text: But when she dies, her brother and their useless father will get to live.

steps.name: Radical Mafioso
steps.text: And she'll bring glory to the famiglia.

steps.name: Radical Mafioso
steps.text: If everything goes nicely, little Luna may even be able to fill her shoes in future. Wouldn't that be nice?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Luna is innocent!

steps.name: Radical Mafioso
steps.text: You had Bellone backing you in the past so we could only turn a blind eye to your antics.

steps.name: Radical Mafioso
steps.text: But the Bellones are history now. Old Bernado's dead. So did you really think we'd just let you do as you please?

steps.name: Radical Mafioso
steps.text: You were the main target all along.

steps.name: Radical Mafioso
steps.text: So if you want to blame someone, Signorina, blame yourself. You shouldn't have taken her in. A truly terrible decision.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Out of my way—

steps.name: Radical Mafioso
steps.text: *tsk* Truly a judge who strikes fear in the famiglie's hearts. Can't underestimate your combat prowess.

steps.name: Radical Mafioso
steps.text: A shame you're here alone.
And what if she has backup?

steps.name: Radical Mafioso
steps.text: What—?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Lavinia, are you alright?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Leon?!

steps.name: Radical Mafioso
steps.text: Why, if it isn't Nuova Volsinii's very own celebrity, Signor Leontuzzo.

steps.name: Radical Mafioso
steps.text: Or should I call you Representative Leontuzzo now?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Whatever you want.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: How did you—

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I heard you were planning to pick up Rubio's body, so I placed some people here to keep an eye out.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Go, Lavinia. I have a rough idea of what's going on, so leave it to me. The girl...

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Only you can save her.

steps.name: Radical Mafioso
steps.text: Leontuzzo. What difference does it make, you being here?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I came prepared, of course.

steps.name: Radical Mafioso
steps.text: *tch* So Texas is here too...

steps.name: Radical Mafioso
steps.text: Stop them!

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: This way.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Grazie.
The crossbow bolt nails Teresa's clothes down.
Luna's eyes are glued to her, but a smile remains on the woman's face.

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: Pretty good shot. You must have pictured this moment in your head so many times, huh?

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: Shut up.

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: If only you could see yourself now, my dear.

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: When I looked into your eyes, I just knew. You're truly one of us.

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: No, that's not it. Rather, is there anyone who isn't one of us?

spans.text: No, that's not it. Rather, is there anyone who

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: Does that judge truly think she's any less base, less filthy than we are?

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: How much blood does she have on her hands?

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: And your father, what a beautiful speech he gave.

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: But how many deaths did he turn a blind eye to?

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: I don't believe it, ragazzina. What makes them think they can build a clean house with dirty hands?

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: Padre's hands are clean, and so are Lavinia's!

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: I won't let you insult them again!
Luna keeps her crossbow aimed at Teresa, but the clerk does not flinch one bit.

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: Insult?

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: I'm only stating the facts.

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: If you truly hate the famiglia that drove Rubio to his death...

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: Then this is your chance.

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: What's wrong, are you scared?

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: Is that all your feelings for your father amount to?

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: SHUT UP!!!

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Luna, stop!

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Ugh...
A sharp crossbow bolt pierces through Lavinia's shoulder.

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: La... vinia...?

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: Wh-Why...?

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: I... I’m sorry...

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: Lavinia?! What are those men doing—

steps.name: Clerk Teresa
steps.text: Ugh...

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Calm down, Luna. And put your weapon down too.
Lavinia covers her shoulder and slowly but surely approaches the girl.
Luna recoils in panic, but doesn't know where to run.

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: She insulted padre. She said he died for nothing.

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: She insulted you too. Said everything you do is meaningless.

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: She deserves to die, just like all the mafiosi!

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: People like her will be punished in the end.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: But if you kill her now, everything will be over.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: The books you borrowed from me, aren't you reading them because you wanted to be a person who can judge others fairly?

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: I know!

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: But, but—!

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: I dream of Papà every day, and I dream of that gunshot!

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: I don't know what to do!

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: I study so hard so I can forget, but I can't!

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: I CAN'T!!!

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: ...Who could forget?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: But the last thing your father would want is for you to act on impulse and forget what we should do, and where we should go.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: He waited decades for his one and only chance.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: He may not want you and I to walk the same path, but I can't just stand by and watch you stain your hands with blood.

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: But I can't help it. There's no way I can...

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: I can't wait that long...

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: I want everyone to know padre wasn't the kind of person they think he was...

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: That day will come, Luna. I promise you.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: And until it does, I'll always be by your side.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Even if I'm the last person in this land to believe in your father's words. I'll keep the faith and fight for it.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Because I share the same dream.
Lavinia walks over to Luna and cradles the crying child in a tight embrace.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: When you can't take it anymore, just come find me.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: I'll listen to your complaints; I'll cry with you.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: And when you're older, we can drink a little vino together as we complain to one another, and bear each other's troubles when we can't handle them alone.

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: I... Can I really?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Of course. But you must promise me you will learn patience.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: You must try to hold it in against anything that angers you.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Alright?

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: I wanted to, I really, wanted to, but, but... I'm so..s-sorry—*sob* Waaaaah!!!!

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: I know, I know.
The crossbow drops to the floor, and the hands that were holding it grab onto Lavinia instead.
Tears well up once more, but this time they wash away the anger and hate.
After a long time, the crying finally stops.
Lavinia wipes away Luna's tears, and carries the unconscious Teresa out the door with the girl by her side.
As they walk, she suddenly seems to recall something, and says—

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: ...I'm sorry, Luna.

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Whether it's me or your father, consciously or otherwise, we've been asking you to become what we want you to be.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: I've met enough people to know that justice and righteousness... are not the only paths one can take.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: But—

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: A long time ago, when I had just started working...

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: I was the same as you, hoping I could knock some sense into the famiglie. I wanted to let them know they can't do as they please.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Then one day, I found myself at the entrance of an alley.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: If not for someone stopping me from going in, I may have died in that very alley.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: That person presented me with a box containing the glove and hammer I wield now.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Back then, I thought that if I hid behind him... I might not be able to stand up for myself for the rest of my life.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: So I took the weapon he gave me and walked ahead of him.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Now that I'm recalling all this, I think that's what he hoped I'd do. And he'd also hope I would do this today.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Mafiosi always treat death like it is inevitable, as merely the result of solving a problem.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: This cycle of violence is how they live and survive.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Long, long ago, a bunch of people walked in the rain into an alley with no lights. They would either die in there, or come out with blood on their hands.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Then, they went further, deeper into the alley, and gradually forgot why they were there in the first place. And in the end, they saw that narrow alley as a full-width street.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Siracusa is a labyrinth of narrow alleys, even dead ends.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: The people living inside the maze don't have many choices to make.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: If the choice was between people like me or the famiglie, I'd rather insist on keeping you by my side.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: But you don't have to become me, and I'm not hoping for that either.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: I'd much rather be able to take you outside this labyrinth entirely.

steps.name: Luna
steps.text: What's outside of it?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Roads. Many wide open roads.
